notes: The image shows 5 jumper wires (red, black, teal, orange, and a short black one) although the parts list says 4; the image is treated as authoritative.
The breadboard image has rows f-j on the top half and a-e on the bottom half. The catalogue puts 'b' bank on rows f-j, so the top half of the image is bank b and the bottom half is bank t.
Button legs are in columns 4 and 6, straddling the centre gap. Column 4 is side 1 (wired to 5V via the orange wire). Column 6 is side 2 (wired to pin 2 and to the pull-down resistor).
The pull-down resistor runs from column 6 to column 9. A short black wire takes column 9 to the ground rail.
Rail hole numbers (bp.1, bp.3, bn.1, bn.7) are estimated from the image. The rail with the red line is positive (bp) and the one with the black line is negative (bn).
The USB cable (for serial communication and power) is not drawn in the circuit image. It is added as a joined edge to the Arduino with no ports.
